actionCards/act.description: Apply a user action to a logged card. Shared checks run first, then the kind reconciles the card; `dismiss` is recorded here and every other verb goes to the card's kind. `dismiss` also works on an unstarted card whose kind is no longer registered. Concurrent actions on one card share one operation.

agentPresets/read.description: Read one declaration's child plugin list as YAML, for viewing only.

agentPresets/select.description: Select a preset before a session starts its first turn. A Session whose log records the preset and whose Agent runs its current revision keeps its composition; nothing is logged or announced.

agentTeams/setEnabled.description: Save a root Session's Team selection without stopping children or deleting tasks. The selection takes effect before awaiting persistence. Tools resolve availability at step preparation; prompt providers read the selection when evaluated. Task mutations check the current mode when their queued operation starts; admitted operations finish.

job/follow.description: Stream one job's retained output from an absolute byte offset, then its terminal projection once settled and drained. Non-consuming: the model-facing cursor and notice state never observe these reads. The request's session is the fenced read's caller; the registry rejects a job the session cannot see and an unknown job.

job/kill.description: Kill one background job on a human's behalf. The request's session is the fenced read's caller, so the job must be one that session can see: the registry's owner fence is the only access rule, and a child session's own jobs are killable from its list like any other. The kill records `cancelled by the user` as its reason; it is not one the model requested, so the owning agent still receives the completion notice, and a shell tool waiting on that job reads the reason in its own result.

job/list.description: Stream the jobs one session can see — its own plus every unowned job — as whole-set frames: one on open, then one after each coalesced burst of lifecycle commits. The stream has no natural end; the carrier closes it.

remoteAccess/follow.description: Stream the calling Peer's access snapshot: one baseline, then `upsert` and `remove` frames after each `invalidate()` and each policy registration or removal that changes a grant. The owner receives only `{ owner: true }`. The generation ends when `signal` aborts or this service unloads, so a reloaded service starts every reader from a fresh baseline.

fileReferences/list.description: List file and directory candidates for one Agent's working directory.

session/attachment.description: Read one image from the attachment store after gateway authorization.

session/cancel.description: Cancel one active Agent turn without dropping its pending inbox.

session/canOpenWorkspacePath.description: Report whether this deployment can hand a Session workspace path to a native desktop.

session/control.description: Stream a complete live-control baseline followed by replacement frames.

session/create.description: Create one ordinary Session for a new conversation, reusing the named blank Session while it is reusable.

session/events.description: Read one cold-safe, message-aligned Session history page.

session/follow.description: Follow one Session log from its opening or resume cursor.

session/fork.description: Fork one cold-readable exact event prefix into a new Session. An omitted boundary selects the latest completed-turn prefix; an open cut receives synthetic fork closers.

session/initializeDefaultModel.description: Select the first available account model after login when no provider API key is configured.

session/list.description: Read all visible Session rows without resuming an Agent.

session/modelCatalog.description: Describe every currently routable model for Host-generation selectors.

session/observeEvent.description: Subscribe to Session events without reading a snapshot.

session/observeState.description: Subscribe to complete Session state replacements.

session/openWorkspacePath.description: Verify one path through the composed filesystem and open it on the Host desktop.

session/page.description: Read one cold-safe, message-aligned Session history page.

session/projections.description: Read exact projections, returning cached hints only when migration is required.

session/prompt.description: Admit one prompt after explicitly resuming its Session.

session/rename.description: Rename one Session after explicitly resuming it.

session/search.description: Search visible Session content without resuming an Agent. A non-owner receives only the hits whose Session `allows()` admits; `hasMore` describes the bounded result before that filtering.

session/selectModel.description: Select one Session-local model after explicitly resuming the Session; save the default in the background.

session/updateQueue.description: Mutate one still-pending queue occurrence, resuming a cold Agent first.

session/wait.description: Wait for Session quiescence or pending input with bounded assistant output.

session/workspacePathApplications.description: Query current file handlers on the serving desktop without activating an Agent.

skills/list.description: List the user-invocable skills visible to one Session composition.

credentials/describe.description: Describe several references for one configuration surface. Batched because a settings page describes every reference its rows name at once, and one round trip keeps those rows from settling separately.

credentials/set.description: Store one value from a configuration surface. The value crosses the wire in this direction only: no read path returns it.

credentials/unset.description: Remove one reference from a configuration surface.

settings/describe.description: Describe every registered namespace for a configuration page: redacted layered values plus the serialized schema the page renders its form from.

settings/mutate.description: Apply path-addressed edits to one namespace's user section, resolved against the section as stored rather than against whatever the caller last read, then answer with that namespace's new redacted view.

settings/openSettingsDocument.description: Materialize the provider-owned settings document and open it in a native text editor.

settings/replace.description: Replace one namespace's stored user section wholesale.

settings/update.description: Merge a patch into one namespace's stored user section.

terminal/attach.description: Attach terminal input and output to one physical Remote stream.

terminal/close.description: Close an identity to future creation and kill its process range; repeated closes succeed.

terminal/create.description: Allocate a user shell once for a caller-generated identity, without Agent sandbox or approval restrictions.

terminal/environment.description: Read the Session's current directory and terminal limits without filesystem validation or shell lookup.

terminal/list.description: List retained terminals without resolving or activating an Agent.

terminal/rename.description: Rename a terminal without changing its shell.

terminal/retain.description: Retain an existing terminal for a window without activating its Agent or taking input control.

terminal/shells.description: Discover installed shells in the Session's execution environment.

terminal/watch.description: Stream the Session's retained terminals as whole sets, without resolving or activating an Agent.

directoryPicker/createDirectory.description: Create one child directory for a Remote caller's in-app browser.

directoryPicker/list.description: List one directory level for a Remote caller's in-app browser.

directoryPicker/pick.description: Open the host's OS chooser for a Remote caller.

workspace/archiveSession.description: Hide one known Session from Workspace grouping surfaces.

workspace/create.description: Create or idempotently resolve one Workspace over an existing directory.

workspace/delete.description: Remove one Workspace registration while retaining files and Sessions.

workspace/follow.description: Stream a complete Workspace baseline followed by ordered increments. A non-owner receives only the Workspaces and Sessions `allows()` admits. When a delivered Workspace is no longer admitted at its next change or the next order change, the stream sends a `replace` frame with the complete filtered state instead of a `remove`, because a Client never resurrects a removed Workspace; a `remove` frame reports a deletion and reaches only a Client that received that Workspace.

workspace/initializeDefault.description: Initialize or reuse the default Workspace during first-use startup. The directory name is fixed, so the Host never renames or relocates an existing default; its initial title is that same name, which browser consumers label in the reader's language.

workspace/insertBefore.description: Move one Workspace within the registry display order.

workspace/insertSessionBefore.description: Move one accounted Session within a Workspace.

workspace/pinSession.description: Surface one known unarchived Session ahead of unpinned Sessions.

workspace/rename.description: Rename one Workspace to a unique non-blank title.

workspace/unarchiveSession.description: Restore one archived Session to Workspace grouping surfaces.

workspace/unpinSession.description: Remove one Session's pin without changing its saved Session order.

workspaceFiles/changes.description: Watch one file or a directory's direct entries in the Session's filesystem. Files use the backend's read authority; directories remain workspace-scoped.

workspaceFiles/list.description: List the direct children of one directory inside the Session's workspace.

workspaceFiles/read.description: Read one page of lines from a UTF-8 file readable by the filesystem backend.

workspaceFiles/readBytes.description: Read a complete regular file or one byte range without text decoding.

workspaceFiles/search.description: Search files and their inferred ancestor directories with packaged ripgrep. Native ignore rules apply unless disabled; VCS metadata, symlinks and empty directories are absent. Within the bounded set of listed files, matches sort by depth, then workspace-relative path.

workspaceFiles/stat.description: Report one regular file's identity, version, and size without its content.

fileUploads/upload.description: Persist one encoded upload and stage it under the Agent receiver selected by Typert.

productAnalytics/report.description: Submit selected Desktop fields with cached static environment and fresh identity. The first intake waits for bounded environment queries; concurrent intakes share them. Missing identity is omitted; failed environment fields carry fixed reasons.

productAnalytics/watchPolicy.description: Stream the effective policy initially and after live configuration edits.

pluginRegistryProbe/fastest.description: Race npm and npmmirror HTTPS ping responses through the Host's fetch proxy. Concurrent readers share a probe; a winner cancels and awaits the other request.

toolResults/watch.description: Observe one committed result without loading a Session or reading its history. Values disappear on count eviction or when the exact Session instance leaves the registry. A cold read stays unavailable; opening a new stream observes the current instance. Inspection does not extend a result's retention.

sessionFeedback/record.description: Record one remark on a live Session.

commands/execute.description: Parse and execute a known command without sending it to the model. A resolved command's lifecycle is logged: `command/run` is appended before the handler is invoked and `command/done` after settlement (a thrown or aborted handler settles as `kind: 'error'`). Both are direct log-only appends — no turn wraps them, and persistence drains them at ordinary checkpoints. Admission misses (syntax or unknown name) log nothing — they never entered a handler. A `command/run` append failure fails the execution loud; a `command/done` append failure on the handler-failure path is contained so the handler's own error stays the reported failure. Attachment admission is enforced here, not in the composer: attachments sent to a command that does not declare `input.attachments`, an absent attachment store, and an exceeded image limit each settle as an error result before the handler runs. Validation rejection starts no attachment writes; a storage failure can leave only unreachable content-addressed objects for deferred collection.

commands/list.description: List the effective immutable command descriptors for one agent.

dynamicCordisRunner/getClientCode.description: Fetch Client code for the exact active run.

dynamicCordisRunner/inventory.description: Frame-wide inventory, grouped as one row per stable Plugin.

dynamicCordisRunner/invoke.description: Invoke an active Host method while rejecting stale Client runs.

dynamicCordisRunner/reportClientGuardFai.description: Report a Client guard rejection that happened after the Package completed activation.

dynamicCordisRunner/reportRenderFailure.description: Record a post-load render failure for the exact active run.

dynamicCordisRunner/resolveInspectQuery.description: Submit a Client inspect result or failure for a pending query.

dynamicCordisRunner/resolveRequestRun.description: Resolve one model-driven Client activation request.

dynamicCordisRunner/runHostHalf.description: Start Host code for an approved request or a direct panel gesture.

dynamicCordisRunner/settleUserRun.description: Settle a direct panel run after this page loaded or failed its Client half.

dynamicCordisRunner/stopFromPanel.description: Stop a Plugin from the user panel and queue the resulting state change for the model's next step.

dynamicCordisRunner/syncInspectManifest.description: Replace the Host mirror of the Client inspect provider directory.

dynamicCordisRunner/undefineFromPanel.description: Remove a Plugin from the user panel and queue the resulting state change for the model's next step.

cuaAccess/applicationIcons.description: Load presentation icons separately from application decisions.

cuaAccess/applications.description: Read fresh stored application decisions without issuing a native request.

cuaAccess/enablePersistentPtc.description: Persist in-memory PTC execution through the existing profile editor and Loader lifecycle.

cuaAccess/openSettings.description: Open the macOS privacy pane selected by the user.

cuaAccess/ptcConfiguration.description: Read PTC execution state separately from native permission checks.

cuaAccess/requestPermission.description: Request the selected system privilege through the native provider.

cuaAccess/retryApproval.description: Clear this application's refusals across sessions so each session may ask for access again.

cuaAccess/revoke.description: Remove saved and session access and join affected operations.

cuaAccess/systemStatus.description: Inspect system privileges independently of application decisions and icons.

account/cancelSignIn.description: Cancel only the named attempt; committing attempts settle before returning.

account/getBalance.description: Query Platform recharge and bonus wallet balances independently of profile data.

account/getNotificationContent.description: Query localized content of a notification, including one already consumed.

account/getNotifications.description: Query unconsumed account notifications in server order without reading profile data.

account/getProfile.description: Query Platform profile independently of wallet balances. A ready result whose stable profile ID first becomes available or changes notifies identity-enabled watch consumers, so they re-read getPlatformSession; repeated IDs stay silent.

account/getState.description: Read stored-account presence and the latest login attempt.

account/reportNotificationEvent.description: Report a notification interaction; the backend decides consumption.

account/signOut.description: Remove the local grant while retaining API keys; the provider revokes it in the background.

account/startSignIn.description: Join an active attempt or start browser authorization.

account/watch.description: Stream account state without the Host-only identity subscription option.

account/watchExpiry.description: Subscribe to live credential expiry without replay.

deepseekChatImport/limits.description: Report the limits the browser checks before uploading. Only the owner may import, so every other principal is refused.

speech/catalog.description: Read provider choices without preparing a recognizer.

speech/follow.description: Follow provider readiness independently of Session and preparation lifetimes.

speech/prepare.description: Start or join one Host-owned preparation task.

speech/transcribe.description: Validate and transcribe one recording through the explicit provider selection.

cotTranslation/limits.description: Read accepted translation preferences and the current request limit without sending text.

cotTranslation/translate.description: Translate one displayed fragment through the reader's selected provider.

forgePanel/branches.description: List the local branches that can start a worktree of the Session's current checkout.

forgePanel/cancelWorktree.description: Withdraw the open worktree request of a Session with its failed attempt, which lets a waiting message go on in the current checkout; without a request the Session is unchanged. Withdrawing needs no worktree service.

forgePanel/changeRequestChecks.description: Load complete checks for the change request whose list the user opened.

forgePanel/changeRequestCommits.description: List the commits of a change request of a Session at its current head, which the changes view can show one or several of instead of the whole change request.

forgePanel/changeRequestDiff.description: Read the changes of a change request of a Session as its code host computes them, with each file's layer following the root `.gitattributes` of the commit the diff ends at. Without `commits` the diff covers the change request at the head commit of its latest status; a patch already read at the same head commit and base branch is reused from memory with its attributes, for any Session, until `maxCachedDiffBytes` evicts it. With `commits`, it covers those commits, from the first one's first parent to the last, and is read every time.

forgePanel/changeRequestReview.description: Read the review threads of a change request of a Session at the head commit of its displayed diff. Threads read at the same head commit and update time are reused from memory, for any Session, until they are `reviewRefreshMs` old, `maxCachedReviewBytes` evicts them, or a review write through this panel drops them; a read again after that age, or a `fresh` read, shows threads resolved elsewhere since, which do not change a GitHub pull request's update time.

forgePanel/changeRequestReviewWrite.description: Write to the review threads or the pending review of a change request of a Session while its head is still the head the user saw. The threads kept for the change request are dropped once the host answers, so the next read shows the write, which a resolve does not show through a GitHub pull request's update time.

forgePanel/changeRequestStates.description: Stream the last known state of every change request that a listed Session the caller may read binds: the stored states first, then each state a poll changes or a new binding reveals. Listing reads no Session log: loaded Sessions report their bindings, others the cached Session summary, and a Session without one shows nothing until it is opened. Closed requests are polled at the idle cadence so reopening is observed. The stream ends when `signal` aborts or the Remote stops.

forgePanel/changeRequestText.description: Read one file of a change request's repository at a commit, which supplies the unchanged lines between the hunks of its diff.

forgePanel/changeRequestViewed.description: Read the signed-in user's viewed marks on the files of a change request of a Session, which the host keeps for the whole change request.

forgePanel/continueInProject.description: Move a Session from its created worktree to the source checkout the worktree came from; the Session no longer works in the worktree. Runs as Agent maintenance, inside the wait of a message that waits for the removed worktree, which then goes on.

forgePanel/diffBases.description: List the branches the `branch` scope of the Session's current checkout can compare with.

forgePanel/dismiss.description: Hide a visible binding of a Session; other URLs leave the Session unchanged.

forgePanel/follow.description: Stream the panel state of a Session: the current state first, then each later state. Intermediate states may be skipped when the reader is slower than the updates. The stream ends when `signal` aborts or the Remote stops.

forgePanel/localCommits.description: List the commits of the `branch` scope of the Session's current checkout, which the changes view can show one or several of instead of the whole scope.

forgePanel/localDiff.description: Read the changes one scope covers in the checkout of the Session's current directory, with Git using the Session's sandbox policy.

forgePanel/localText.description: Read the new side of one changed file in a scope, which supplies the unchanged lines between its hunks: the index for `staged`, the last chosen commit for chosen commits of the `branch` scope, else the working tree.

forgePanel/markReady.description: Mark a draft change request of a Session ready for review; the change request is polled again once the host answers.

forgePanel/merge.description: Merge a change request of a Session while its head is still `headSha`; the change request is polled again once the host answers.

forgePanel/refresh.description: Reinspect a followed Session's checkout, probe sign-in again, and poll its change requests at once; an unfollowed Session is unchanged.

forgePanel/requestReviews.description: Request reviews of a change request of a Session from more reviewers; the change request is polled again once the host answers.

forgePanel/requestWorktree.description: Ask for a new worktree before the Session's first turn, replacing an open request and forgetting a failed attempt. While the next message waits in the inbox, or else at the first step proposal, the panel creates a branch from `from`, or from HEAD of the current checkout when it is null, and enters its checkout. A message that already waits after a failed or stopped attempt keeps waiting for {@link ForgePanelController.retryWorktree}.

forgePanel/rerunChecks.description: Rerun the failed checks of a change request of a Session while its head is still the commit whose checks the user saw; the change request is polled again once the host answers.

forgePanel/restoreWorktree.description: Check out the created worktree of a Session again at its recorded directory when that directory is gone: its branch when the branch still exists, otherwise a new branch of the same name at the base commit. Changes that were never committed are not recovered. Runs as Agent maintenance, inside the wait of a message that waits for the restoration, which then goes on; without a missing directory the Session is unchanged.

forgePanel/retryWorktree.description: Make another attempt, with a new branch name, at the worktree a message of the Session waits for after a failed or stopped attempt.

forgePanel/reviewerCandidates.description: List accounts a review of a change request of a Session can be requested from.

forgePanel/setFileViewed.description: Set or clear the signed-in user's viewed mark on one file of a change request of a Session.

forgePanel/stopCreation.description: Stop the creation a message of the Session waits for; the message keeps waiting with the request still open. Without such a creation the Session is unchanged.

forgePanel/submitReview.description: Publish a line comment or completed review for a visible Session binding. The threads kept for the change request are dropped once the host answers, so the next read shows the comments.

forgePanel/track.description: Bind a change request to a Session by URL, or restore a dismissed binding.

forgePanel/updateBranch.description: Bring the base branch's new commits into the head branch of a change request of a Session while its head is still `headSha`; the change request is polled again once the host answers.

forgePanel/worktreeCleanup.description: Read or await the worktree service's archive cleanup of the Session's checkout.

liveshareShares/capabilities.description: Read the endpoints plugins currently offer.

liveshareShares/create.description: Publish one Session and store the share.

liveshareShares/identity.description: Report this host's owner identity for one Liveshare server address.

liveshareShares/list.description: Refresh titles and Liveshare server authority, then list this host's shares.

liveshareShares/relay.description: Read the Liveshare server address the owner saved.

liveshareShares/setCapabilities.description: Replace one share's exposed plugin endpoints.

liveshareShares/setRelay.description: Choose the Liveshare server address later shares publish to.

liveshareShares/stop.description: Stop one share locally, revoke its forks, and delete its row on the Liveshare server when reachable.

liveshareShares/testPublish.description: Register one throwaway share to check whether this host may publish.

liveshareShares/testRelay.description: Check that the effective Liveshare server answers at all.

liveshareShares/updatePermissions.description: Change one share's tier, fork switch, or both.

goals/clear.description: Clear the current goal while retaining a durable tombstone and history.

goals/complete.description: Mark a current non-complete goal complete and disarm it.

goals/create.description: Create one Goal through the remote boundary.

goals/edit.description: Edit objective and/or round cap without changing phase.

goals/get.description: Read the current goal for one exact live agent.

goals/pause.description: Pause an active goal and disarm automatic continuation.

goals/resume.description: Resume and arm a stopped goal, or rearm an active goal after a session-start edge, while its round budget still has capacity.

pluginInventory/list.description: Read the Loader directly on every call. Cordis's internal plugin/status events already maintain Entry.fiber and Fiber.state, so a second cache would only add another lifecycle truth to keep synchronized. When an agent-preset roster is composed, the snapshot also carries each preset's composition rows, because those rows — not the Loader's own entries — are where a deployment that mounts the roster runs its model-facing plugins.

llm/discoverModels.description: Remote adapter for one draft provider interrogation.

llm/listConfigurableProviders.description: List every declared configurable provider, registered or dormant.

llm/listProviders.description: Describe provider routes with a registered adapter.

mcpManager/probe.description: Probe one server for a management surface; see {@link McpServerManager.probe}.

mcpManager/restart.description: Rebuild one server from its current entry: dispose the live instance (if any) and mount a fresh one with a fresh reconnect budget. Incomplete cleanup blocks replacement until the Host restarts.

mcpManager/watch.description: Stream server views for a management surface: the current list on subscription, then the complete list again after each status or entry change.

messageFeedback/delete.description: Delete one item after checking its version; absence succeeds without an event.

messageFeedback/list.description: Read current feedback from the canonical log.

messageFeedback/put.description: Create or replace feedback after checking its current version. Matching no-ops retain the version and append no event.

officeKit/generation.description: Read the current rendering generation before reusing a Client PDF.

officeKit/render.description: Read and convert one Office file using the Session's ordinary filesystem authorization.

permissionPresets/catalog.description: Read the complete process-level catalog exposed to current-session UI.

pluginManager/cancelInstall.description: Stop an installation this manager owns and wait until its files are back.

pluginManager/inspect.description: Read what a spec names before installing it.

pluginManager/installBundle.description: Install a package using the same pnpm implementation as dsh plugin. GitHub repositories get a connection check bounded by githubConnectionTimeoutMs before pnpm starts; only network failures or timeouts stop installation, and a stop streams the check's diagnostic as the installation's install-log run under its request id, while pnpm owns authentication and transport fallback. An HTTP(S) Git URL on another host is installed over SSH instead when access probes bounded by gitTransportTimeoutMs find that only SSH can read it. A run that fails, is cancelled, or adds a package without a bundle patch restores `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` as they were; downloaded files can stay.

pluginManager/listBundles.description: Read installed, installation-provided, and offline Official catalog bundles, plus selected non-bundle names. A dependency without a bundle patch is listed, as a `not-bundle` problem, only while it is selected.

pluginManager/listPlugins.description: Read current plugins, including why a row cannot be changed through the profile patch.

pluginManager/listVersionExemptions.description: Read exact plugin-version exemptions saved in this profile.

pluginManager/listVersions.description: Read the published versions newer than an installed registry package's version, from the first registry that answers. Official bundles follow the DSH version and are not listed.

pluginManager/readBundleDetail.description: Read a bundle's long description: the Markdown file its locale `meta.detail` names in `language`, otherwise its README. An installed bundle is read from its directory without network access; an official bundle the installation offers before it is installed is read from the npm file CDNs at its offered version. Nothing is cached.

pluginManager/registries.description: Read the registries this manager asks: the configured first one, its fallbacks in order, and what pnpm's own configuration names.

pluginManager/removeBundle.description: Unload and remove a profile-owned bundle dependency through dsh plugin's pnpm path; a selected name no dependency holds is only deselected.

pluginManager/setBundleEnabled.description: Select or remove a bundle layer while retaining installed dependencies.

pluginManager/setPluginEnabled.description: Persist a plugin entry's desired enablement and apply it on live profiles.

pluginManager/setVersionExemption.description: Grant or revoke one exact plugin/runtime exemption and reevaluate live plugins.

pluginManager/updateBundle.description: Replace an installed bundle with a newer version. A registry copy updates to `name@version`, checked on the registry first: it must exist, declare a bundle, and accept the running DSH version, or nothing changes. A Git copy updates to the Git spec `options.spec` names, which must pin a full commit of the repository directory the copy came from; with HMR, a network failure or timeout reaching its repository stops the update before anything changes. pnpm reads a Git package only while installing it, so its bundle and compatibility are checked then. Either target installation is undone, profile files and modules included, before its bundle loads unless it installs `name` at `version`. With HMR the installed version is removed, so its plugins stop, and the target is installed with the same selection; when that installation fails or is cancelled, the removed version is installed again: a registry copy from the registry it came from, a Git copy from its saved spec. Without HMR the target is installed over the running version and the result reports the restart.

pluginManager/waitForInstall.description: Recover the result of an active installation without cancelling it.

pluginMarket/listIndexes.description: List the configured index sources without fetching them.

pluginMarket/readEntryDetail.description: Read the long description of one listed version of a plugin market entry, from the version's source: the npm file CDNs for a public npm version, or its pinned Git commit. The Markdown file the package's locale `meta.detail` names in `language` comes first, then the package's README, then the README of the entry's `repository`, or for an npm version without one, of its `package.json` `repository`, at the default branch. An npm version from another registry has no readable package files, so only the entry's `repository` is read.

pluginMarket/search.description: Return one page of the plugins of a configured index that match a query. Concurrent reads of a URL share one fetch; a successful document is reused for `cacheTtlMs` unless `refresh` is set. Matching and ordering read only the document; installation status and compatibility are computed for the returned page on every call.

pluginMarket/setIndexes.description: Replace the configured index sources through Settings, without remounting this service. `plugin-market/changed` announces the committed list. A URL already configured is kept as written, so a client can add or remove sources beside one that `listIndexes` reports as unusable.

pluginRecommendations/describe.description: Read the current catalog text for a logged card.

schedule/catalog.description: Read every Host task without a page bound or Session activation.

schedule/create.description: Create one task with a Host-generated identity for a human Remote caller.

schedule/deleteInactive.description: Delete every ended Host task, leaving active tasks armed. Ended tasks never schedule another delivery, so the removal changes no pending target and no timer is recomputed. Rows are enumerated and removed in one FIFO slot, so a delivery ordered behind this call ends its task after the enumeration rather than during it. The batch is one domain write: a normal failure rejects with every listed row still stored, while a backend `unknown-state` failure may have removed rows and quarantines the Host domain, so later schedule operations reject until the domain is reopened. A successful nonempty batch emits `schedule/changed` without Agent notices. A rejected batch announces `schedule/changed` because it does not establish which rows landed, and clients then re-read the catalog.

schedule/deliveryLimits.description: Read effective delivery limits without loading or activating a task.

schedule/edit.description: Update or delete one task for a human Remote caller; an invalid patch rejects with `schedule/input-invalid`.

schedule/history.description: Remote form of the target-based {@link ScheduleService.history}; an invalid limit rejects with `schedule/input-invalid`.

schedule/list.description: Remote form of the shared Host-wide list.

schedule/run.description: Deliver one task now without consuming or moving its scheduled occurrence; an archived destination Session rejects with `schedule/target-archived`.

schedule/view.description: Read one task without activating its target Sessions.

sessionReferenceResolver/candidates.description: Remote face of {@link listCandidates}: the configured candidate limit applies, and every candidate carries the canonical mention a host inserts into the prompt draft.

subagents/interruptByUser.description: Remote face of {@link interrupt}, authorized on the target Session by the Gateway. No catalog, history, persistence, or parent Agent lookup runs. Absent, idle, and already-completed targets are accepted no-ops there.

subagents/prompt.description: Deliver one browser-authored message to a continuable child through its live subagent tree root, retaining the caller-minted request identity and validated browser zone on the accepted message. Success identifies the message the child's inbox accepted; later execution is independent of this call. Queue delivery targets a later turn; steer delivery targets the nearest step and retains the Agent loop's best-effort fallback semantics. Image parts are admitted and persisted through the attachment store before delivery, and the child's model must accept image input. Cold resume at capacity rejects with `subagent/delivery-unavailable`. Access is checked on the target Session before attachment admission or restoration.

userQuestions/answer.description: Answer a continued question. The reply is steered into the agent as a user message whose source names the call; that message is also the record that closes the question in the projection.

userQuestions/attachWait.description: Let one answer UI hold a live timed wait. Closing the stream releases its claim.

web/listProviders.description: List every registered search and fetch provider for provider pickers. Availability does not filter the lists.
